lines.quote: as Iran looms large, can the GOP keep the faithful? approval 36% amid the war; the Senate map through deep-red states keeps the GOP alive
lines.note: THE DOOR: the war as the page's weather ('looms large'), the voters as 'the faithful' — the denomination is in the hed; the number is in the dek
lines.zWhy: a faithful to be kept at 36% is a price the holder's audience is still paying

lines.quote: two electorates in these midterms
lines.note: THE TITLE — the page's frame: one electorate reading the price, one not
lines.zWhy: two electorates are a price felt by one and discounted by the other

lines.quote: the first is frustrated with Trump and ready to reject Republicans — independents, rural, Hispanic voters
lines.note: the first electorate, by group; the price not yet named
lines.zWhy: an electorate ready to reject is a price not yet down for it

lines.quote: House polling: Democrats up 11 on the generic ballot last week; Fox's national poll
lines.note: the record — the NYT/Siena number (also on MS NOW and NPR 10-27, owed/blocked) in the RI corner's own mouth
lines.zWhy: an eleven-point generic lead is a price read as costing votes, by the corner paying

lines.quote: the second is wavering but may not hand Democrats the Senate — Midwest voters by one or two points
lines.note: the second electorate; the price absent from its description
lines.zWhy: a wavering electorate reads neither way on the pump

lines.quote: declining approval and the Democrats' issue advantages will likely give them the House, possibly by many seats
lines.note: the thesis; 'issue advantages' is the price before ¶17 names it
lines.zWhy: issue advantages that take the House are a price the opposition owns

lines.quote: any Senate path runs through states Trump won by 11+ points; steep against a loyal turnout
lines.note: the slate's geometry; the price absent — vacancy
lines.zWhy: a steep path reads neither way on the pump

lines.quote: the answer in seven days
lines.note: the clock, dated — the only date on the page that is not a poll's
lines.zWhy: seven days is a window the holder's 'soon' has to fit

lines.quote: Trump has overcome nearly every threat in eleven years; the exception the pandemic, which led to the Biden presidency
lines.note: the page's most denominated line: the holder's career as the frame, the price nowhere — vacancy; the author's Rule 5 peak
lines.zWhy: a career of threats overcome reads neither way on the pump

lines.quote: the pandemic one of the few foreign-origin threats he has faced
lines.note: the analog the author reaches for — a foreign-origin threat that cost an election; vacancy (the price still unnamed)
lines.zWhy: a foreign-origin threat as the analog is a war read as the pandemic was

lines.quote: Iran the new foreign opponent; the February decision to launch joint strikes has weighed on the GOP
lines.note: the force dated to February and read as the weight — the author's own cause
lines.zWhy: a war that weighs on the party is a price not yet lifted by the deal

lines.quote: approval 44% in the last pre-war survey → 36% now
lines.note: THE GAP, DATED: eight points between the last pre-war poll and this one — the page's lowest-Dia line with ¶17–¶18
lines.zWhy: eight points lost since the war is a cure not yet felt by the room

lines.quote: Iran tied to four top issues: inflation 85%, gas prices 83%, government leadership 79%, the war 75%

lines.quote: Democrats preferred +16 on inflation, +12 on gas prices, +11 on leadership, +9 on foreign policy
